steps.title: A sends the Request over LA
steps.html: Function 1 in Endpoint A is the Requester, the Function that initiates the transaction. On LA, A's Port is the Transmitter and Switch Downstream Port A is the Receiver. The Request moves upstream, toward the Root Complex.
steps.condition_html: The teaching example reads host memory and receives one Completion. Arbitration, replay, and unrelated traffic are omitted.

steps.title: The Switch forwards the Request over LR
steps.html: The Switch sends the Request from its Upstream Port to the Root Port. The transmitting and receiving Ports have changed, but Function 1 in A remains the original Requester. Internal forwarding does not add an external Link.
steps.condition_html: The observation point moves from LA to LR. The Switch forwards this Request rather than originating another transaction.
steps.source_html: Base 6.0 §1.3.3／Figure 1-3，p.107；§2.2.6.2，p.157 — the Switch preserves the Transaction ID。

steps.title: The host-side Completer returns a Completion over LR
steps.html: The Completer, the Function that handles the Request and produces its response, is on the Root Complex side. The Root Port now transmits and the Switch Upstream Port receives. Traffic moves downstream; the Upstream Port keeps its topological name.
steps.condition_html: The example assumes the Read was handled and a data response is being returned. A transfer on one Link alone is not evidence that every transaction succeeded.

steps.title: The Completion returns to A over LA
steps.html: Switch Downstream Port A transmits the Completion and A's Port receives it. Function 1 in A is still the original Requester, now receiving its response. Requester does not mean the end currently transmitting a packet.
steps.condition_html: This is the return path of the same Read. Completion-field and integrity checks are developed in the transaction chapters.

caption_html: Author-created sequence diagram based on the cited rules. Read from top to bottom; spacing does not represent measured latency. Solid arrows cross LA or LR; dashed arrows show internal Switch forwarding. DP and UP mean Downstream Port and Upstream Port.
order_html: Follow the Request from A to the host, then the Completion back. Reassign the transmitting and receiving ends for each Link transfer. LA and LR are the Link labels used in this chapter.
summary_html: Port names follow topology. Transmitter and Receiver follow a particular transfer. The Requester for the same Read does not change when it starts receiving its Completion.
